profiles.summary: Endpoints on 2026-11-24 report bor v2.11.1-private (publicnode), v2.11.1 (QuickNode), v2.11.2 (OnFinality) and v2.11.0 (1rpc). The 12 hex field that earlier cycles read as a build commit is the node identity, which bor sets to the host name, and Polygon states that v2.11.1-priv and the public tag v2.11.1 are the same code. A pre-release v2.12.0-beta of 2026-11-23 adds a MULMOD reciprocal memo on the path FullMath.mulDiv takes and an opt-in keccak cache for inputs up to 8 KiB; both compute the specified results as read.

deltas.delta: The middle field of the bor client version (a863b8e5cce1, f2a2d63e69f6, cb3d19c5f690 on publicnode; qn-tsw-fra-10093 on QuickNode; a Kubernetes pod name on OnFinality) is the node identity. bor's default Identity is Hostname() (internal/cli/server/config.go line 923, function at lines 2307-2313 at tag v2.11.1), which in a container is the 12 hex character container id. It is not a commit, which is why none of the three ids resolves on GitHub.

Polygon announced on 2026-11-16 that bor v2.11.1 is the public release of v2.11.1-priv with identical code, that the private build reports 2.11.1-private and the public build 2.11.1. The public tag is commit 1567556 of 2026-11-13. QuickNode now reports the public v2.11.1.

bor v2.12.0-beta (pre-release, 2026-11-23, commit 350427e) routes MULMOD with a modulus whose top limb is nonzero through a one-entry per-EVM memo of (modulus, reciprocal) and calls uint256.MulModWithReciprocal (core/vm/mulmod_memo.go lines 55-66, core/vm/instructions.go lines 200-205, core/vm/interpreter_dispatch.go lines 134-143). FullMath.mulDiv uses the modulus 2^256-1 on every call (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24), so on a node that runs this release every swap and liquidity change takes the memo path. Polygon tells mainnet operators to wait for v2.12.0, and no endpoint queried runs it.

bor v2.12.0-beta adds the flag --precompile-cache (default off). With it on, the serial importer and the block builder share the per-block caches with the parallel workers and the prefetcher, and KECCAK256 of 1 to 8,192 bytes is cached in a sync.Map keyed by the whole input as a string (core/vm/shared_cache.go lines 162-241, core/vm/instructions.go lines 284-328). The pull request notes that the serial run is then no longer an independent re-execution, and a failed cached serial run is retried once without caches (core/blockchain.go lines 1436 and 1497-1499).
1rpc.io/matic reports bor v2.11.0 and polygon.api.onfinality.io answers 429 to the battery's calls; neither could be used for vector runs this cycle.

profiles.summary: bor v2.11.1's parallel state pins the first multi-version read of an account's code for the rest of the transaction, so the two code reads that resolve a delegated account cannot see two versions. Mined liquidity removals and fee collections match the source to the unit.

deltas.delta: ParallelStateDB.readCodeKey caches the first MVHashMap read of CodePath per address and per transaction (core/state/parallel_statedb.go lines 170-177 and 365-377). The comment names the case the cycle 11 critic raised: resolveCode and resolveCodeHash of a 7702 delegated account following different delegation targets and poisoning the shared jump destination cache. GetCodeHash of code set earlier in the block hashes the bytes it read (cachedCodeHash, lines 871-887 and 899-907), and the per-transaction hash memo is dropped on SetCode (line 949) and on the revert of a create (parallel_statedb_journal.go lines 93-104).

findings.title: BNB Chain's own RPC nodes run a geth build whose commit is not in the public repository
findings.difference: bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org and bsc-dataseed2.bnbchain.org answer web3_clientVersion with Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104. The v1.8.2 tag is commit 54afaff4 of 2026-11-03. GitHub returns not found for the compare view v1.8.2...4e1c8247 and HTTP 422 for the commit, while the tag commit and the later pre-release commit 4bd1c730 resolve. The geth version string appends the first 8 characters of the build commit and the build date, so the official endpoints run code built one day after the release from a commit the public repository does not hold.
findings.mechanism: Every BSC reading of cycles 8 to 12 (interpreter, jump destination cache, keccak opcode, state) used the public v1.8.2 tag. A build from an unpublished commit can differ in any of these. The vectors and scripts of this cycle ran against that build and gave the specified results, so whatever differs is outside what 185,529 opcode vectors, 8,415 MULMOD sequence vectors and the PoolManager scripts reach. The most likely explanation is a private security or operational patch on top of v1.8.2, as BNB Chain has shipped before, which nobody outside can read.
findings.impact: No loss path. The difference is that the code serving BNB Chain's own endpoints, and possibly its validators, cannot be read, so the source readings of this review cover the public release only.
findings.preconditions: None for the fact. A harmful difference would need BNB Chain or a validator to run a faulty private build.
findings.mitigations: Ask BNB Chain which commit 4e1c8247 is and whether validators run it, and rerun the vector and script sets after Jenner on 2026-12-08 against both dataseed and reth-bsc.

sources.supports: web3_clientVersion returned Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 on 2026-11-24, and dataseed2 the same
v1.8.2 is commit 54afaff, released 2026-11-03; tmp-master-4bd1c730-20261117 is a later pre-release

the tag commit resolves (54afaff4da31ac9e49ba646a4f65104edac5a2f3, 2026-11-03), while https://github.com/bnb-chain/bsc/commit/4e1c8247 returned HTTP 422 and https://github.com/bnb-chain/bsc/compare/v1.8.2...4e1c8247 returned not found

findings.title: Bor v2.12.0-beta puts a reciprocal memo on the MULMOD that FullMath runs on every swap, and an opt-in keccak cache in front of every mapping slot
findings.difference: bor v2.12.0-beta, a pre-release published on 2026-11-23, replaces the stock uint256.MulMod in both interpreter loops with a one-entry memo of the last full-width modulus and its reciprocal, and with --precompile-cache it caches KECCAK256 results of 1 to 8,192 bytes per block across the prefetcher, the parallel workers, the serial importer and the block builder.
findings.mechanism: FullMath.mulDiv computes mulmod(a, b, not(0)) on every call (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24) and mulmod(a, b, denominator) when the product exceeds 256 bits (line 48); mulDivRoundingUp adds one more (line 112), and SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta one (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252). The modulus 2^256-1 has a nonzero top limb, so on this release it always takes the memo. The memo compares the whole four-limb modulus (mulmod_memo.go line 57), stores Reciprocal(z) on a miss and then calls MulModWithReciprocal, which in uint256 v1.3.2 runs exactly the umul and reduce4 calls that MulMod runs with a freshly computed reciprocal (uint256.go lines 688-748); reduce4 only reads the reciprocal (mod.go lines 334-381), and the destination-equals-modulus aliasing is the same as in the stock opcode. The memo is a field of the EVM, and each BlockSTM incarnation builds its own EVM (core/parallel_state_processor.go lines 132 and 628), so no two goroutines share it. The keccak cache keys on the full input bytes and stores the hash by value (shared_cache.go lines 196-241), so a hit is the hash of the same bytes. As read, both changes compute the specified results. They matter for deployment because they put new code on paths every pool operation takes (mulDiv and the mapping slots of src/libraries/Pool.sol, Position.sol and TickBitmap.sol:67-70), the memo carries state from one MULMOD to the next for the whole block, and with the flag on the serial run stops being an independent check of the parallel one.
findings.impact: None as read. If a later version of the memo or cache were wrong, swap amounts, fee growth or slot addresses would be computed differently on the nodes that run it, which would show first as a consensus split between bor versions.
findings.preconditions: Validators or RPC operators would have to run v2.12.0-beta or a later release with this code; Polygon tells mainnet operators to wait for v2.12.0. The keccak path also needs --precompile-cache.
findings.mitigations: Rerun battery.py, targeted.py, this cycle's mulmod_memo.py and the PoolManager scripts against a v2.12.x node before validators adopt it, and keep --precompile-cache off on nodes that serve as independent verifiers.

sources.supports: v2.12.0-beta pre-release of 2026-11-23, commit 350427e, highlights MULMOD reciprocal caching (#2310) and the --precompile-cache flag (#2431), and tells mainnet operators to wait for v2.12.0
MulModWithReciprocal and MulMod run the same reduce4 call, lines 688-748; bor pins uint256 v1.3.2 in go.mod line 59
with the flag on the serial processor reads the same caches, and a failed serial run is retried without caches

cleared.check: Opcode battery (99,985 vectors) and targeted set (85,544 vectors) rerun on 2026-11-24 against six endpoints: bor v2.11.1-private (polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com), bor v2.11.1 public tag (rpc-mainnet.matic.quiknode.pro, new since cycle 9), BSC geth v1.8.2-4e1c8247 (bsc-dataseed1, an unpublished commit), reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f (bsc-rpc.publicnode.com), and avalanchego 1.15.3 on api.avax.network and publicnode.
cleared.result: Every vector that ran returned the specified word: 185,529 of 185,529 on five endpoints and 184,929 on api.avax.network, where 600 vectors were refused with HTTP 429 and ran in full on the second Avalanche endpoint. No mismatch. OnFinality (bor v2.11.2) and 1rpc (bor v2.11.0) refused the calls with rate limits.

cleared.check: pmdiff (250 scripts, 12,322 PoolManager calls, Ethereum reference with the same reference hashes as opcodes/pmdiff.json) on the public bor v2.11.1 build and the unpublished BSC build; pmdiff2 (300 scripts with hook and token doubles) on the BSC build.
cleared.result: BSC dataseed1 (4e1c8247): 250 of 250 and 300 of 300 identical to Ethereum. QuickNode bor v2.11.1: 231 of 250 identical, and the 19 that differ are exactly the 19 indices recorded for Polygon in opcodes/pmdiff.json and attributed to the 25 million gas cap on a swap across most of the tick range.

cleared.check: MULMOD sequences built for the reciprocal memo of bor v2.12.0-beta: 8,415 records in one call per batch, with runs of one full-width modulus, alternation of two, moduli one limb or one bit away from the previous one, narrow and zero moduli between them, 2^256-1 as FullMath uses it and the 512 bit product of FullMath.mulDiv.
cleared.result: All six endpoints (two bor v2.11.1, BSC geth, reth-bsc, Avalanche, Ethereum) gave the specified word for every record that ran, 8,415 each and 7,415 on api.avax.network after two batches hit HTTP 429. No endpoint runs v2.12.0-beta, so this is a baseline for the rerun the memo needs, not a test of it.

cleared.check: Does the MULMOD memo of bor v2.12.0-beta give the stock result for every input, including FullMath's modulus 2^256-1, destination equal to modulus, and state carried between calls, frames and transactions of one EVM.
cleared.result: Yes as read. The memo compares all four limbs of the modulus before reuse and recomputes Reciprocal(z) on a miss (core/vm/mulmod_memo.go lines 55-66). MulModWithReciprocal and MulMod in uint256 v1.3.2 run the same umul and the same reduce4 call (uint256.go lines 688-748), reduce4 only reads the reciprocal (mod.go lines 334-381), and opMulmod aliases destination and modulus in the same way in both versions (instructions.go line 202 at v2.11.1 and v2.12.0-beta). Moduli with a zero top limb and a zero modulus take the stock call. Each parallel incarnation constructs its own EVM (core/parallel_state_processor.go lines 132 and 628), so the unsynchronised memo is not shared between goroutines. The ruint 1.21.0 fault class (OPCODES.md) does not apply: bor uses holiman/uint256.

cleared.check: Can the widened keccak result cache of bor v2.12.0-beta (--precompile-cache) return a hash for another input, for example across lengths or after EVM memory changes.
cleared.result: No as read. Keys are string(data) over the whole input, so inputs of different length or content never share an entry; Load builds a non-retained string view, Store copies the input and stores the hash by value with LoadOrStore, and a full cache stops inserting rather than evicting (core/vm/shared_cache.go lines 162-241). The 64 byte legacy path is unchanged from v2.11.1, which cycle 11 cleared.

cleared.check: Can the ecrecover result cache of bor v2.11.1 be poisoned through an eth_call or eth_simulateV1 that overrides the precompile at 0x01, a hole that v2.12.0-beta closes with precompilesOverridden.
cleared.result: Not on the import path of v2.11.1: the shared ecrecover, keccak and jump destination caches are created per block in newSharedBlockCaches and applied only to the import prefetcher and the parallel workers (core/blockchain.go lines 1268-1289); the RPC path creates no shared cache. The PoolManager makes no ecrecover call in any case.

cleared.check: Lead L-646 for BSC geth v1.8.2: is any code-derived cache shared across transactions or workers and keyed by a code hash read apart from the code.
cleared.result: BSC adds a process-wide LRU of jump destination bitmaps keyed by code hash (core/vm/contract.go lines 27-30, used in isCode lines 99-112), which every EVM of the process shares, including the prefetch workers. Each EVM runs on one StateDB copy in one goroutine (core/state_prefetcher.go lines 71-121), and Call takes the code and its hash from that StateDB with no execution in between (evm.go lines 355-363 and resolveCode / resolveCodeHash at lines 700-724). The account's code hash is the hash of the stored code, so every bitmap is stored under the hash of the bytes it was computed from. Init code is analysed under the zero hash and never stored (evm.go line 631). Pooled Contract objects clear the cached analysis on reuse (contract_pool.go line 36).

cleared.check: Lead L-646 for reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix: where is the jump table of a contract computed and can it belong to other bytes.
cleared.result: revm-bytecode 10.0.0 computes the jump table inside Bytecode::new_legacy from the raw bytes and stores it in the same Bytecode value (bytecode/mod.rs lines 128-134, legacy/analysis.rs lines 10-36). There is no separate code hash key for the analysis, so a jump table always belongs to the bytes it travels with.

The jump destination map is created fresh for a top-level call and passed to child frames only (core/vm/contract.go lines 64-72), so it lives for one transaction's call tree on one StateDB and is never shared between transactions or goroutines.

cleared.check: Lead L-659: shift and byte handlers of revm-interpreter 35.0.1 over ruint 1.18.0, which is inside the range of RUSTSEC-2026-0220.
cleared.result: BYTE indexes only below 32 and SHL, SHR and SAR call ruint only for a shift below 256 after as_usize_saturated, returning zero or the sign fill otherwise (instructions/bitwise.rs lines 96-143). The advisory's wrong overflow flag and modulo 2^32 amount therefore cannot be reached through these opcodes. The battery and targeted sets pass on the endpoint.

cleared.check: Keccak bucket test of theme-keccak-cache (36,059 inputs of 1 to 88 bytes grouped by the bucket index of the alloy-primitives cache, sent interleaved in three rounds) on reth-bsc, which runs the cache, and on BSC geth and Avalanche as controls.
cleared.result: 108,177 of 108,177 hashes equal the Python keccak on each of the three endpoints, no error.

cleared.check: Mined swaps, newest window: Polygon blocks 97,883,631 to 97,885,397 and BNB Smart Chain blocks 135,481,689 to 135,485,688, with a step by step replay of the multi-step and crossing swaps.
cleared.result: Polygon: 1,608 swaps, all pass the tick relation, 1,384 of 1,417 pairs match a single step to the unit, and all 25 sampled multi-step swaps replay to the unit (up to 20 steps). BNB Smart Chain: 9,460 swaps, all pass the tick relation, 8,218 of 8,264 pairs match a single step, and the 25 sampled multi-step swaps and the 2 swaps that crossed liquidity (206 steps) replay to the unit.

cleared.check: The cycle 11 critic's concern for bor v2.11.1: under BlockSTM, can resolveCode and resolveCodeHash of one Call read two versions of a delegating account's code, so that a bitmap is stored in the block-shared jump destination cache under another contract's code hash.
cleared.result: Not as read. ParallelStateDB.readCodeKey stores the first MVHashMap read of each address's code for the rest of the transaction (core/state/parallel_statedb.go lines 365-377), and the field comment names this exact case (lines 170-177). For code written earlier in the block, GetCodeHash hashes the bytes returned by that same cached read (lines 899-907, cachedCodeHash lines 871-887); for pre-block code both reads come from the same base state. The per-transaction hash memo is dropped on SetCode (line 949) and on revert of a create (parallel_statedb_journal.go lines 93-104). The deeper questions of the code theme (prefetcher views, entries written by incarnations that later fail validation) are left to that unit; given the pinning, an entry is computed from the bytes it is keyed by whichever incarnation wrote it.

cleared.check: Lead L-656: amounts paid on mined liquidity removals and fee collections, by the transaction-level method of theme-mined-liquidity (analyze2.py), on Polygon (BlockSTM producers), BNB Smart Chain (two clients) and Avalanche.
cleared.result: Polygon blocks 97,844,995 to 97,884,994: 302 transactions checked, 293 match principal plus fees to the unit, and the 9 others are rebalancing transactions in one JPYC pool where a small positive delta (797 to 9,999,999,974,048 wei of an 18 decimal token) left no Transfer log and the PoolManager's JPYC balance did not change across the block, which is a clear of dust (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319) and not a payment by the producer. BNB Smart Chain blocks 135,480,349 to 135,484,348: 275 checked, all exact; 3 native-BNB transactions could not be checked because no endpoint serves debug_traceTransaction. Avalanche blocks 101,116,887 to 101,267,286: 40 checked, all exact. Every predicted storage word of positions, ticks and pool liquidity equalled storage at the block on all three chains.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses published since cycle 9: Polygon's security review of 2026-11-24 (v2.10.3 BlockSTM denial of service, Karwar, Uburu), bor v2.11.1's stateless import header checks, reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix's upstream state root fix, the BEP-706 sample code issue raised on the BNB forum, avalanchego v1.15.1 to v1.15.3 fixes (snapshot generation blocking SAE execution, builder ordering).

The bor items are liveness bounds that Polygon states do not change execution results; the reth-bsc fix concerns the state root of a legacy path and is in the build the endpoint runs; the BEP-706 issue concerns contracts that read 0x70, which the PoolManager does not; the Avalanche fixes are performance and ordering. leadResults.answer: The 12 hex fields are not commits. bor sets the node identity to os.Hostname() by default (internal/cli/server/config.go line 923 and lines 2307-2313 at v2.11.1), which in Docker is the container id, so a863b8e5cce1, f2a2d63e69f6 and cb3d19c5f690 name containers; QuickNode's and OnFinality's fields are host and pod names in the same position. The -private suffix is the private distribution: Polygon's announcement of 2026-11-16 says v2.11.1-priv and the public v2.11.1 (tag commit 1567556, 2026-11-13) are the same code, that the private build reported 2.11.1-private, and that most validators ran it. Polygon's 2026-11-24 review describes the same process for v2.10.3-priv and v2.11.0-priv. QuickNode now serves the public v2.11.1 build, which passed the battery, the targeted set and pmdiff with the same results as the private build. The readings of cycles 9 to 11 from the public tag therefore apply to what the endpoints and, by Polygon's statement, validators run.

reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix is commit 23b510f8, the one bsc-rpc.publicnode.com reports. Its Cargo.lock pins revm 38.0.0, revm-interpreter 35.0.1, revm-bytecode 10.0.0, ruint 1.18.0, alloy-primitives 1.6.0 and fixed-cache 0.1.10. keccak-cache-global is on: the crate depends on bnb-chain/reth v0.1.4 with default features (Cargo.toml line 19), whose bin/reth/Cargo.toml lists keccak-cache-global in default and forwards it to alloy-primitives (lines 83-91, 120-124). That is the alloy-primitives 1.6.0 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 text cycle 11 read for X Layer. battery.py (99,985) and targeted.py (85,544) passed on the endpoint, and the keccak bucket test gave 108,177 of 108,177 correct hashes. The shift handlers clamp before calling ruint, so RUSTSEC-2026-0220 is not reachable through SHL, SHR, SAR or BYTE.
